title: Had house valued today by 3 Estate Agents - 50K difference
key_point: Valuations £105k-£170k; others report £40k-£150k spreads; seller who chose highest valuation later reduced to lowest; check sold prices, Mouseprice.

title: Disaster - HSBC have valued the flat at 20k under what I offered
key_point: East London flat: asking £275k, offer £280k, lender £260k; surveyors use sold not asking prices; renegotiate, top up, or walk.

title: Offers over, guide price, offers in excess of etc
key_point: Offers over/guide/OIEO read as agent uncertainty; English buyers often pay below (e.g. £15k under); Scottish convention differs.

title: Sell house at offers above or higher asking price
key_point: Consensus: conventional asking price beats 'offers over', which buyers dislike; overpricing risks lender down-valuation; one exception sold £134k vs OO £130k.

title: Feedback for London flat
key_point: WC2B flat ~£800k with Foxtons: layout, dated decor, lease under 100 years; posters suggest ~£650k; Foxtons seen as overpricing.

title: Where are all the property buyers
key_point: West Drayton maisonette, 96-yr lease, online agent: few viewings; new-build oversupply, Brexit, season; switching to high-street brought viewings.

title: Estate Agent Valuations
key_point: Unique house, no comparables for 8 years: four agents ~£225k, one £180k; pick agent on track record; list near midpoint.

title: Selling my London flat: which agent?
key_point: London 1-bed: earlier 25% overvaluation failed; six quotes £310k-£335k; fees 1.25-1.75%+VAT vs Purplebricks £1,400; short tie-ins advised.

title: Estate agent valuation or surveyor
key_point: Surveyors are qualified valuers, agents are not and may inflate; ask agents for 'quick sale' figure; lenders use Esurv, Connells, Countrywide.

title: How are houses really valued?
key_point: Agents use printed comparables; location dominates; £/sqft starting point in cities; configuration matters; new kitchens add little value.

title: Range of Valuations - SE London. Confused.
key_point: SE London: four valuations £525k-£600k; KFH highest and locally known to overvalue then reduce; seller chose realistic £550k agent.

title: Is my house overpriced?
key_point: Asking £435k vs identical £400k comparable; £30k upgrades add little; 4 viewings in 3 weeks weak; advised cut to £400-415k.

title: Anyone buying or selling in SE London at the moment? How's the market?
key_point: SE London £700-800k homes sold within a month, within £25k of asking; agents pre-market test at inflated prices; railways/small gardens linger.

title: Advice on down-valuation
key_point: South London flat: asking £580k, offer £550k, lender £520k; seller refused; buyer tried second lender; post-COVID flat demand weak.

title: Should I accept lower offer for my London flat?
key_point: N14 373 sqft studio: valuations £200k-£265k; listed £265k, cut £260k; best offer £250k; studios niche; SDLT April 2025 timing.

title: My flat won't sell - help!
key_point: North London 1-bed share-of-freehold cut £50k; no outside space, EWS1/cladding fears, service charges, buyer exodus from London flats.

title: Are sold prices always correct on Rightmove?
key_point: Rightmove sold prices are lagged Land Registry data; shared ownership, transfers and errors distort comparables.

title: OIEO query
key_point: Zone 2 London flat: agent insisted OIEO £450k vs seller's £465k; 15 viewings, one offer; market signalled overpricing.

title: Rightmove vs Zoopla valuation
key_point: Automated valuations diverge wildly (106% vs 58.6%; £1.093m vs agent £1.5m); data errors; buyers decide price.

title: Seller reject survey valuation?
key_point: Sellers weigh lender valuation more than buyer's survey; gaps often split (£10k down-valuation settled at £5k); depends who is more desperate.

title: Purplebricks vs local estate agent
key_point: Mixed online-agent experiences: ghosting buyers vs one-week sale at asking; local agents ~1-1.6%+VAT; online needs seller effort.

title: Best and final - how high do people actually go?
key_point: Best-and-final bids 2-12% over asking; agents favour proceedable buyers; overbids risk mortgage down-valuation.

title: High-street estate agent or online?
key_point: High-street negotiation can pay its fee; some buyers avoid online listings; counterexample: Yopa got offers after 16 offerless high-street weeks.

title: Drop in value of leasehold flats (all types) in last 5-7 years - trend to continue?
key_point: Leasehold flats stagnant/falling (£300k to £280k; £167k to £95k) while houses rise; service charges, cladding, short leases, reform uncertainty.

title: Impossible to sell flat with extortionate service charge
key_point: Sydenham conversion: service charge £1.5k to £6k (£10k proposed); asking £465k cut to £350k; sold 2020 £325k.

title: London flat market
key_point: Zone 2-3 flats without outside space unsellable; service charges to ~£8k, cladding, lease length depress values; share-of-freehold conversions do better.

title: Estate agents at odds over overvaluing to win instructions
key_point: GetAgent: 95% see rivals overvalue, 89% lost instructions to higher valuers; drivers: sellers, competition, targets; agent commenters critical.

title: Agents increasingly turning to high property valuations to win instructions
key_point: Agent Software data: overvaluing to win instructions rising; overvalued homes linger and weaken vendor negotiating position.

title: Selling a property: the priciest estate agents are most likely to overvalue
key_point: Times/Zoopla: biggest agents overvalue most, charge ~2x commission; a third of listings cut avg £23,400 (6.9%).

title: Estate agents are significantly over-pricing houses by up to £82,000
key_point: 89,582 sales: asking-sold gap largest in SW London £82,100, NW London £80,299, W London £59,192.

title: London buyers hit by sharp rise in surveyor markdowns
key_point: Down-valuations rising on London flats in large blocks: thin comparables, stale agent pricing, landlord sell-off; family homes near schools hold up.

title: Fraud: agents who deliberately over-value to win instructions act illegally
key_point: Headline claims deliberate overvaluing to win instructions is illegal; page returned 403, content not read.

title: Over valuations
key_point: Thread body loads via JavaScript; not readable; snippet suggests agents over/undervalue to win instructions.

title: Estate agents told to stop over-valuing homes to gain instructions
key_point: Snippet: allAgents says almost half of valuations inaccurate; a trainer advocates over-valuing; commenter says corporates use the strategy.

title: Selling a flat with viewings but no offers
key_point: Snippet claims roughly one offer per seven viewings; unverified.
